verdict.rationale: Airbyte documents a public API for programmatically controlling Airbyte, including orchestration from tools like Airflow, which implies triggering and monitoring syncs. However, the pack never shows specific job-status, failure-log, or re-trigger endpoints. Failure diagnosis (logs, errors) is documented only in the UI Connection Timeline, and the MCP server evidence covers agents accessing data rather than managing pipelines. Missing for 10: explicit API endpoints for job status and re-running syncs, API or MCP access to failure logs/diagnostics, an MCP server exposing pipeline operations, and hands-on corroboration of an agent doing this loop.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can check sync status, diagnose a failed run, and re-trigger it through an API or MCP server

citations.quote: Use the Airbyte API to programmatically interact with Airbyte. For example, you can control Airbyte in conjunction with orchestration tools like Airflow.
Programmatically control Airbyte Cloud, OSS & Enterprise.
You can also view and download logs, find any relevant errors
